title: kith-jmap: ResultReference resolver (RFC 8620 §3.7)
description:
ResultReference resolver: evaluate RFC 6901 JSON Pointer back-references in JMAP batches before method dispatch.

What: Implement pub fn resolve_references(method_calls: &mut Vec<Invocation>, prior_responses: &[(String, serde_json::Value)]) -> Result<(), JmapError> that substitutes ResultReference values before dispatch.

Algorithm:
1. For each invocation at index i in method_calls:
   a. Take the args serde_json::Value (index 1 of the tuple)
   b. Scan the args object for keys starting with '#' (e.g., '#ids')
   c. For each such key:
      - Parse the value as ResultReference (result_of, name, path fields)
      - Look up result_of call_id in prior_responses (only indices < i); if not found → return Err(JmapError::invalid_arguments("resultOf references unknown call_id"))
      - Verify the method name in prior_responses matches the ResultReference.name field; if mismatch → return Err(JmapError::invalid_arguments("resultOf name mismatch"))
      - Call serde_json::Value::pointer(&path) on the prior response value; if None → return Err(JmapError::invalid_arguments("path does not resolve"))
      - Insert resolved value into args using the key without the '#' prefix
      - Remove the '#'-prefixed key from args
2. Return Ok(())

RFC 6901 rules handled by serde_json::Value::pointer():
- Path segments separated by '/'
- '~1' → '/' in key name
- '~0' → '~' in key name
- Integer segments for array indexing

Defensive programming rules:
- Never unwrap() pointer result — return typed error
- Only look backward (indices < i) — forward references are an error
- A referenced call that returned an error is invalid (its value may be an error object, not a data value); detect by checking if value has 'type' key at root
- Mutate args in place; do not silently skip invalid references
- No key material involved

Tests (oracles from RFC 8620 §9):
- Simple path /list/0/id resolves to first item's id field
- Nested path /foo/bar/0/baz resolves correctly
- Path to nonexistent field → Err invalidArguments
- Array index out of bounds → Err invalidArguments
- Forward reference (result_of references later call) → Err invalidArguments
- Reference to error response → Err invalidArguments
- Escaped path with ~1 resolves slash in key name
Oracle: All test vectors hand-constructed from RFC 8620 §9 examples and RFC 6901 §5, not derived from resolver code.
